# Standalone AI & Programmatic API Specification (`api/API.md`)

Authoritative specification for the standalone authenticated FastAPI service under `/api/` (`api/`), designed for AI agents and programmatic clients while the browser IDE runs separately under `/webapi/` (`webapp/API.md`).

## 1. Architectural Overview & Reverse-Proxy Routing

The `api/` package provides a read-only, token-efficient REST service independent of the browser-facing `webapp/` server:

- **Process separation**: `api/main.py` runs on its own port (`127.0.0.1:8001` by default) via `python3 api/main.py` or `uvicorn api.main:app`, while `webapp/main.py` serves the browser IDE and `/webapi/*` on port `8000`.
- **Anubis reverse-proxy split**: External bot/AI protection (Anubis) sits in front of `webapp` (`/`, `/b/*`, `/webapi/*` -> port `8000`) and bypasses `/api/*` straight to port `8001`, where `api/security.py` enforces API key authentication, progressive IP lockout, and sliding-window rate limiting on every request.
- **Zero unauthenticated surface**: FastAPI interactive docs are disabled (`docs_url=None`, `redoc_url=None`), OpenAPI schema discovery lives behind auth at `GET /api/openapi.json`, and `CORSMiddleware` is omitted so browser cross-origin preflights or wildcard `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` headers are never emitted.
- **Service & DB reuse**: Endpoints in `api/routers/v1.py` reuse `webapp/backend/services/*`, `webapp/backend/database/pool.py` (`with get_reader() as reader:`), `webapp/backend/config.py` (`RepoContextMiddleware` and `require_feature`), and `webapp/backend/security/` (`jail.py`, `git.py`, `sql.py`). All database access stays strictly read-only through `db_engine`.

## 2. Configuration & CLI Execution

Settings live under the `"api"` section of `config.json` (`core/config.py`, `config.example.json`), resolved with precedence `CLI Flags > Environment Variables > config.json > Built-in Defaults`:

| Key | Default | Env Var | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `host` | `"127.0.0.1"` | `API_HOST` | Bind address for `api/main.py` |
| `port` | `8001` | `API_PORT` | Listen port (`1`–`65535`) |
| `reload` | `false` | `API_RELOAD` | Auto-reload toggle for uvicorn |
| `default_version` | `"v3.0"` | `API_DEFAULT_VERSION` | Default revision when `version` query param is omitted |
| `keys` | `[]` | `API_KEYS` / `KIP_API_KEYS` | List of non-empty strings or `{name: key}` mapping (empty fails closed) |
| `rate_limit.max_requests` | `120` | — | Maximum authenticated requests per `window_seconds` per key and per IP |
| `rate_limit.window_seconds` | `60` | — | Sliding-window duration in seconds |
| `auth_lockout.max_failures` | `5` | — | Missing or invalid key attempts within `failure_window_seconds` before lockout |
| `auth_lockout.failure_window_seconds` | `60` | — | Sliding failure counting window in seconds |
| `auth_lockout.base_lockout_seconds` | `30` | — | Initial temporary ban duration in seconds (doubles each consecutive lockout) |
| `auth_lockout.max_lockout_seconds` | `3600` | — | Maximum progressive lockout duration cap in seconds |
| `trusted_proxies` | `["127.0.0.1", "::1"]` | `API_TRUSTED_PROXIES` | Trusted proxy IPs or CIDRs allowed to supply `client_ip_header` |
| `client_ip_header` | `"X-Forwarded-For"` | `API_CLIENT_IP_HEADER` | Header read when direct peer IP is in `trusted_proxies`: `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`, or `CF-Connecting-IP` (case-insensitive; any other value normalizes to `X-Forwarded-For`, `normalize_api_client_ip_header()`) |

File logging is `logging.api` (`core/config.py`, same keys as `logging.webapp`): `enabled` (`false`), `dir`, `file` (`"api.log"`), `request_mode` (`"all"` or `"errors"`), `error_dir`, `error_file`, `level` (`"INFO"`), overridable by `KIP_API_LOG_ENABLED`, `KIP_API_LOG_DIR`, `KIP_API_LOG_FILE`, `KIP_API_LOG_REQUEST_MODE`, `KIP_API_LOG_ERROR_DIR`, `KIP_API_LOG_ERROR_FILE`, `KIP_API_LOG_LEVEL`. `create_app()` and `api/main.py` call `setup_api_logging()` (`core/logging_setup.py`), which attaches the `api` target exactly like the webapp target (request-mode filter, uvicorn loggers, stdio capture).

A standalone service configuration is `config_api.json` (`API_CONFIG_FILENAME`, `get_service_config_path("api")`). `ensure_standalone_config("api")` seeds it once from `config.json` through `prune_api_config()`, which keeps only `database` (with `ssh_tunnel`), `cache`, `workspace`, `repositories` (without parser `preparse` rules), `api`, and `logging.api`, and sets `api.reload = false`.

CLI entrypoint (`api/main.py`):

```bash
python3 api/main.py [-c config.json] [--host 127.0.0.1] [--port 8001] [--reload | --no-reload]
uvicorn api.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001
```

## 3. Authentication, Anti-Brute-Force Lockout & Rate Limiting

`api/security.py` implements pure ASGI middleware (`ApiAuthMiddleware` and `ApiRequestLoggingMiddleware`) without `BaseHTTPMiddleware` so `ContextVar` repository state propagates to sync and async handlers:

1. **Trusted proxy client IP extraction (`extract_client_ip`)**:
   - Forwarding headers are honored only when `scope["client"][0]` belongs to `api.trusted_proxies`; untrusted peers always resolve to their direct socket IP.
   - For `X-Forwarded-For`, hops are walked right-to-left skipping `trusted_proxies`, picking the rightmost untrusted valid IP and falling back to the direct peer IP if malformed.
2. **Pre-auth IP lockout check**:
   - Evaluated before reading or verifying API keys so locked-out IPs immediately receive `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After` without leaking key validity (blocking even valid keys during the cooldown).
3. **Constant-time API key verification (`verify_api_key_constant_time`)**:
   - Reads `X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
   - Hashes the presented key and every configured key with SHA-256 and compares the fixed-length digests with `hmac.compare_digest`, scanning all keys without short-circuiting (neither key length nor match position affects timing).
   - Empty or missing `api.keys` fails closed (`401` on all requests).
4. **Failure counting & progressive exponential lockout**:
   - Both missing and invalid API keys increment the per-IP failure counter and return generic `401 {"detail": "Invalid or missing API key"}`.
   - Reaching `max_failures` within `failure_window_seconds` triggers a temporary ban of `min(max_lockout_seconds, base_lockout_seconds * 2**(tier - 1))`.
   - Authenticating with a valid key clears the IP's failure streak (`_ip_failures.pop(client_ip, None)`).
   - Tracked IP and key maps are LRU-bounded (`MAX_TRACKED_IPS = 4096`, `MAX_TRACKED_KEYS = 4096`) to prevent memory exhaustion under IP churn.
5. **Authenticated sliding-window rate limits**:
   - Enforced independently per `key_id` and per `client_ip` (`429` + `Retry-After`).
6. **Redacted request logging & security headers**:
   - `SecurityHeadersMiddleware` wraps all responses (including early `401` and `429` rejections).
   - `ApiRequestLoggingMiddleware` logs via `api.request` using only key names (`key=<name>`), never logging `Authorization`, `X-API-Key`, or raw configured secret values.

## 4. Curated REST API Endpoints (`/api/v1/*`)

All endpoints honor `X-KI-Repo` or `?repo=<name>` (`RepoContextMiddleware`), default `version` to `api.default_version`, enforce per-repo feature flags (`require_feature`), validate inputs (`safe_rev`, `resolve_and_verify_repo_path`, `validate_pathspecs`, `is_valid_identifier`), and include pagination (`limit`, `offset`) plus `truncated: bool` where responses are bounded:

| Group | Endpoint | Feature | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Discovery** | `GET /api/openapi.json` | — | Authenticated OpenAPI 3 schema |
| **Discovery** | `GET /api/v1/capabilities` | — | Compact service summary, repos, features, limits, and endpoint catalog |
| **Repos** | `GET /api/v1/repos` | — | Configured and auto-detected repositories |
| **Repos** | `GET /api/v1/branches` | — | Paginated Git branches of active repository |
| **Repos** | `GET /api/v1/versions` | — | Paginated tags and indexed versions (`q`, `indexed_only`, `include_rc`) |
| **Repos** | `GET /api/v1/status` | — | Active repository ingestion status |
| **Code** | `GET /api/v1/tree` | — | Paginated directory listing (`version`, `path`) |
| **Code** | `GET /api/v1/files/search` | — | Fuzzy file path search (`q`, `version`) |
| **Code** | `GET /api/v1/file` | — | Bounded line slice (`path`, `version`, `start_line`, `end_line`, `limit`) |
| **Code** | `GET /api/v1/file/outline` | — | AST/symbol outline (`path`, `version`) |
| **Code** | `GET /api/v1/file/imports` | — | `#include` directives and optional `resolve_header` lookup |
| **Code** | `GET /api/v1/file/references` | — | Includers, Kconfig `source`s, docs, and Kbuild rules referencing `path` |
| **Symbols** | `GET /api/v1/symbols/search` | — | Symbol definition prefix search (`q`, `version`) |
| **Symbols** | `GET /api/v1/symbols/definition` | — | Ranked definition (with optional local scope via `from_file`, `line`, `col`) |
| **Symbols** | `GET /api/v1/symbols/references` | — | Paginated categorized cross-references (`name`, `version`, `arch`) |
| **Symbols** | `GET /api/v1/symbols/hover` | — | Hover signature, location, and kernel-doc |
| **Symbols** | `GET /api/v1/symbols/ast/{ast_id}` | — | Recursive AST container subtree (`depth`) |
| **Symbols** | `GET /api/v1/struct` | `pahole` | Struct/union memory layout, member offsets, holes, and cachelines |
| **Symbols** | `GET /api/v1/callgraph` | `callgraph` | Paginated callers and callees of `function` |
| **Symbols** | `GET /api/v1/callpath` | `callgraph` | Shortest call chains between `from` and `to` |
| **Search** | `GET /api/v1/grep` | — | Bounded `git grep` (`q`, `mode`, `case`, `word`, `path`, `per_file`) |
| **History** | `GET /api/v1/commits` | `commits` | Commit search and structured `git log` query |
| **History** | `GET /api/v1/commits/{commit_hash}` | `commits` | Commit metadata, trailers, and touched files |
| **History** | `GET /api/v1/commits/{commit_hash}/diff` | `commits` | Bounded structured diff of a commit |
| **History** | `GET /api/v1/blame` | `commits` | Bounded `git blame` line range (`path`, `start_line`, `end_line`) |
| **History** | `GET /api/v1/history/file` | `commits` | Chronological commit history of a file |
| **History** | `GET /api/v1/diff` | `compare` | Bounded diff between `version_a` and `version_b` (file or tree summary) |
| **Knowledge** | `GET /api/v1/kconfig/search` | `kconfig` | Search Kconfig symbols by name or prompt |
| **Knowledge** | `GET /api/v1/kconfig/symbol/{symbol_name}` | `kconfig` | Kconfig symbol definition, dependencies, help, and optional usage |
| **Knowledge** | `GET /api/v1/kconfig/build` | `kconfig` | Kbuild compile conditions for up to 64 source paths |
| **Knowledge** | `GET /api/v1/kconfig/eval` | `kconfig` | Evaluate repeated `symbol` values and `path` Kbuild conditions under `defconfig` (default: the arch default) plus repeated `assign=NAME=value` edits (`KconfigService.evaluate()`) |
| **Knowledge** | `GET /api/v1/maintainers` | `maintainers` | Maintainer lookup by `path`, `section`, or `q` |
| **Knowledge** | `GET /api/v1/docs` | `docs` | Kernel-doc extraction for `path` or `Documentation/` label search (`q`) |
| **Knowledge** | `GET /api/v1/man` | `man` | Linux man-pages lookup (`name`, `section`, `path`, `version`, `kernel`) |
| **Knowledge** | `GET /api/v1/cve` | `cve` | Paginated CVE catalog or per-file CVE lookup (`file_path`) |
| **Knowledge** | `GET /api/v1/cve/{cve_id}` | `cve` | Single CVE record with commit ranges and optional `release` state |

`GET /api/v1/kconfig/eval` loads the configuration `make ARCH=<arch> <defconfig>` writes (`load_config()` + `set_all_new_symbols("default")`, `parser/kconfig_ast/KCONFIG_API.md` §8.3), applies each `assign` with kconfig's setter rules (`set_value()`; refused or undefined names are listed in `rejected`), and returns `symbols` (`{value, type, defined, visible, changeable}` per name) and `files` (each path's Kbuild condition `expr` with its tristate `result`: `"y"`, `"m"`, `"n"`, or `"?"`, `parser/kbuild_conditions.py` `evaluate()`). Limits: 128 symbols, 64 paths, 128 assignments.

Not exposed: `checkpatch`, asynchronous `insights` jobs, `watch`, `nodemap` layouts, and `patch_apply` (heavy, unsafe, or UI-only); there is no MCP server.

## 5. Operations: Systemd, TUI Launch & Reverse Proxy

- **Systemd**: `core/systemd_manager.py` manages `kernelinfo-api.service` (`API_SERVICE_NAME = "kernelinfo-api"`, `API_UNIT_NAME`) beside the daemon and webapp units (`VALID_SERVICES = ("daemon", "webapp", "api")`). `ExecStart` runs `python3 api/main.py --config <config_api.json>` directly (`Type=simple`) or inside tmux (`Type=forking`, socket and session `kernelinfo-api`). Preflight warns when the configuration has no `api` section or no `api.keys` (every request would answer `401`).
- **Configuration TUI** (`core/API.md` §7.3): `ScopedConfigMenuScreen("api")` edits `config_api.json` (`ApiSettingsScreen` in `core/tui/screens/api_cfg.py`: server, masked keys, limits, trusted proxies, client-IP header; `LoggingScreen` for `logging.api`), and `SystemdServicesScreen` installs and controls the API unit.
- **Foreground launch**: main-menu item `W` (`Launch Webapp / API Servers`) asks for *Webapp only*, *API only*, or *Both*, resolves unsaved edits with `choose_launch_config()`, and exits the TUI with `{"servers": [...], "config_path": ...}`. `pipeline/cli.py` `arg_handling()` hands that to `launch_servers()` before the parser's memory guard and logging: each server runs as `python3 <entry> -c <config>` in its own process group; SIGINT/SIGTERM are forwarded to every server, one server exiting stops the others, and a server still running 15 s (`SERVER_STOP_GRACE_SECONDS`) after the stop signal is killed.
- **Reverse proxy & Anubis**: route `/api/*` around Anubis directly to the API port (`8001`) and everything else (`/`, `/b/*`, `/static/*`, `/webapi/*`, `/sw.js`, `/manifest.json`) through Anubis to the webapp port (`8000`). The proxy must reach the API from an address in `api.trusted_proxies` and set `api.client_ip_header` (overwriting, not appending to, any client-supplied `X-Real-IP` / `CF-Connecting-IP`; appending to `X-Forwarded-For` is safe because hops are read right-to-left). Without a trusted proxy hop, lockout and rate limits key on the socket peer, so a proxy outside `trusted_proxies` would make every client share its address.
